title: Who were the Vikings?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore who the Vikings were, responding to a listener request from David D. of Waterloo. They cover the Viking Age (roughly ninth to eleventh centuries) as a profession of raiding rather than an ethnic group, Scandinavian geography and motives for expansion, pre-Christian Norse religion (Aesir and Vanir, Odin, Thor, Valhalla, Valkyries, Ragnarok), the meaning of "going Viking" and theories on the word's origin, Viking ships and naval skill, raiding and enslavement of thralls, burial customs, berserkers and the mushroom and bear-cult theories, Viking democracy and the assembly (the Thing and the lawmaker), Viking settlements in Ireland, England, Normandy and Newfoundland (Leif Ericson, Eric the Red), Viking games including a ping-pong-like game and a hurling-like ice game, pop culture references (Thor, Led Zeppelin, Deadliest Warriors), and myths about Viking hygiene and skull drinking. The episode ends with a plug for a Worlds of Wayne interview and a listener-mail-style "list of firsts" from Patrick.
topics: Viking settlements in Ireland and England

segments.title: Opening banter and studio move
segments.summary: Hosts joke about recording in a temporary office during studio renovation, then introduce the Viking topic with a question about the Minnesota Vikings helmet horns.

segments.title: Listener request and when Vikings existed
segments.summary: The episode is a listener request from David D. of Waterloo. The hosts say Vikings were active in Europe from the ninth to eleventh centuries and that Viking was a profession of raiding rather than an ethnic group, with Scandinavians also being farmers and weavers.

segments.title: Why Vikings raided: population and geography
segments.summary: Hosts describe Scandinavia's harsh climate and limited arable land, along with population growth, as motives for Viking expansion and plundering. The eleventh century roughly marks the adoption of Christianity.

segments.title: Norse pagan religion and mythology
segments.summary: Vikings were pagans with a personal religion and no central church. The hosts describe the Aesir and Vanir gods, Odin and Thor, Asgard and the rainbow bridge, giants and dwarves, and the prophesied battle of Ragnarok.

segments.title: Valhalla and going Viking
segments.summary: Warriors who died in battle were carried to Valhalla by Valkyries to fight and feast with Odin. The hosts explain that going Viking meant leaving home to raid, and describe raiding churches for gold and taking thralls.

segments.title: Origin of the word Viking
segments.summary: The hosts list theories for the word Viking, including Old English wic meaning trading port, Norse vik meaning bay, a word meaning to turn away or leave on a journey, and an Old Norse word meaning pirate that Europeans may have supplied.

segments.title: Viking ships and seamanship
segments.summary: Vikings were skilled seamen with fast double-ended, keeled, riveted longships with a single square sail and shields along the sides. The hosts describe the attacks on monasteries and towns, and the burning and taking of people and livestock.

segments.title: Viking weapons, iron, and funerals
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Viking weapons and armor such as swords, bows, lances, javelins and iron helmets, and Scandinavian skill with bog iron. They describe ship burials and mound burials, including servants and possessions buried with the dead.

segments.title: Berserkers and the mushroom theory
segments.summary: Berserkers are described as warriors possibly tied to a bear cult, who fought in frenzy without feeling pain. The hosts discuss the theories that they used magic mushrooms or mead, and that some may have been mentally ill, and mention the Clerks reference.

segments.title: Viking democracy and expansion abroad
segments.summary: Viking-era Scandinavians held assemblies called things with a lawmaker as impartial judge. The hosts describe Viking settlements in Dublin and Ireland, the Danish control of parts of England, the Normandy deal with Charles the Simple and Rollo, and voyages to Greenland and Newfoundland by Eric the Red and Leif Ericson.

segments.title: Viking games and leisure
segments.summary: Hosts describe Viking socializing, including competitions like running, wrestling and horseback riding, entertainers, a shield-based game similar to ping pong called kinky bat, and a bone-skate ice game similar to hurling.

segments.title: Vikings in popular culture and myths
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Thor in Marvel comics, Adventures in Babysitting, Led Zeppelin's Viking-inspired songs, and the TV show Deadliest Warriors. They then address myths that Vikings were dirty, drank from conquered skulls, and had horned helmets; they bathed weekly.

segments.title: Show plugs and Worlds of Wayne
segments.summary: Hosts plug an interview they did on the Worlds of Wayne podcast and invite listeners to search the HowStuffWorks site for more on Vikings.

segments.title: Patrick's list of firsts
segments.summary: Hosts read a list from listener Patrick of the show's firsts, including the first podcast episode, first listener mail, first bleeped swear word, and first over-forty-minute episode, and discuss the new studio.

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts ask for berserk stories to be emailed to the show and close the episode.
